decision: Root ADR-0317 §5.2: the one-time move of both price tables' vintages into their versions tables. The job unit_price_versions_migration (orchestration/jobs.v1.json) runs it, one bounded run at a time; this file is how a run is sized and cut. infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs/vintage_versions.py reads it (load_contract), and scripts/ops/unit-price-versions-migrate.sh takes the Spark size from it.

spark.$reason: The compose `spark` service (20g cap) the price lane and the Gold rebuilds use with the same settings (hub-building-register-apartment-price-source-objects.json silver_refresh.spark, gold-panel-rebuild.contract.json). The job takes all three spark slots, so nothing shares the cap.

$run_time_budget: A step (one shard of one vintage's write, or one vintage's parity check) starts only while the elapsed run time plus that step's cost stays within this budget: 90% of the job's 160-minute time_limit_minutes (jobs.v1.json). 160 is the most a job taking all three spark slots may hold them: one minute more and the map-edit folds may wait past 20 of their hourly runs (orchestration/dags/job_specs.py pool_starvation), the bound gold_panel_rebuild sits at. A step's cost is the figure below until the run has taken a step of that kind, then the longest such step of the run. A step in flight is never cut; the next run starts from the first step not recorded.
$parity_buckets: The parity check compares, per bucket of the key's hash, the row count and two 64-bit sums of each row's key-and-content hash (data-diff's checksum segments). Only a bucket whose checksums differ is compared row for row (exceptAll), so an equal vintage is two narrow aggregations, never a shuffle of its rows.

targets.$measured: write: 2026-11-04 the first vintage (202608, 202,102,050 rows, 5.73 GB appended) committed 13,226 s after the run started at 11:11:38Z (Iceberg $snapshots 14:52:04Z), beside gold_panel_rebuild (11:37-14:17Z) and the onbid and rt-molit Silver loads the pool did not count; a vintage is written in 4 key-hash shards of a quarter of that each (3,307 s), so a shard fits a run with room for a parity check. parity: before the checksums, the 202608 check (rows_as_of ranked over the wide rows, then exceptAll both ways, each a shuffle of all 202M rows with raw_columns) ran 15,574 s from that commit to the kill at 19:11:38Z without finishing, beside lakehouse_maintenance (its 18:26:45Z rewrite of this table). With the checksums: computed, one read of the vintage's partition and of the versions as of it, narrowed to the key and two hashes, plus two 4,096-row aggregations. The vintages after the first are compared with the versions (release_changes); the first is its rows (vintage_changes first), so 202609 and 202610 are planned at the first's figure until a run measures one.

computed: one batch of silver.unit_official_price is 188.7M narrow rows (0.50 GB of 3.14 GB, Iceberg $files 2026-11-04); the table is partitioned by sido, so a batch's read scans the whole 3.14 GB once.
